data.narrative:
LabGenius is a seed-stage biotech company founded by James Field that has raised $73M to date. The valuation analysis relies on a limited comp universe: three public peers in Biotech & Health (RXRX, TEM, ONT.L) and eight private companies in the sector, though none provide sufficient overlap on stage, timing, or valuation tier for reliable peer-median benchmarking.

Given data constraints, only the stage-progression method is applicable. Using total capital raised ($73M) as a proxy for seed-stage valuation, a $27M base value is escalated by a 2.5x multiplier—the typical step-up to the next financing round—yielding $68M. This method captures the dilution and value-accretion trajectory between seed and Series A stages in venture biotech.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $57M to $78M, with a median of $68M. The low-end estimate assumes conservative round-step assumptions; the high-end reflects more aggressive scaling scenarios. Key limitations constrain precision: the absence of same-stage comparable companies; no disclosed revenue for LabGenius, precluding public multiple application; and reliance on a single triangulation method rather than convergent approaches. The public biotech P/S median of 5.6x could theoretically anchor a valuation if revenue were available, but this remains unmeasured. Investors should treat this range as indicative pending disclosure of financial metrics or emergence of tighter private comparables.
